data.narrative:
Silicon Quantum Computing, led by founder Michelle Simmons, is a Series A quantum computing company that has raised A$83M to date. The quantum computing sector includes 3 public comps (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private peers including Quantinuum, IonQ, PsiQuantum, D-Wave Quantum, and SandboxAQ.

The valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method due to data constraints. Stage-progression methodology applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to the A$83M raised proxy, implying a valuation of $166M. A peer-median approach proved inapplicable; while 8 same-sector peers exist, none satisfied narrow filtering criteria (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier), and a broader all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given quantum computing's heterogeneity in business model and maturity.

The triangulated range spans $141M (low) to $191M (high), with a median point of $166M. This narrow range reflects reliance on a single methodology rather than strong convergence across methods. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 2.0x multiplier for this specific stage transition in quantum computing, where funding rounds may not correlate predictably with valuation step-ups, and the absence of direct peer comparables limits validation of the implied valuation against market precedent. Further diligence on recent Series B fundings in the peer set would strengthen conviction in this range.
